issue: #587 — Flat reversion P5 blocker (retire the counted publication receipt chain and the on-chain tx-field-receipt-v1 validator), on spec #565. Rows first pinned by #577 (family rebind lane C, transition-trace/Q21), re-taken by #584, and re-taken here for the one row #587 moves.
spec: docs/spec/midgard-tx.md §4, §7.1, §7.3, §8.8, §10 — fields 0 and 2 of a disputed L2 transaction read through the §8.8 door under authenticate-once, and the forced-order path re-derived from the transaction id alone
note:
Lane C's rolling re-measurement, attached as this lane's exit criterion per #565's measurement-slotting rule (AC3), and **re-taken under #584** — the issue #577 opened specifically to beat the L2 row it had to publish as a regression. Both rebound call sites are pinned rather than only the one that improved.

What the rows measure. `validate_l2_transaction_transition` opens field 0 (spend inputs) and field 2 (outputs) through the §8.8 door instead of decoding each preimage and re-hashing the reproduced item list; `tx_order_compact_body` re-derives the compact body from the transaction id instead of verifying the retired proof-source triple.

Movement, against HEAD b824ad6e as #577 measured it. The L2 row `accepts_valid_l2_transaction_no_op_transition_fault` went 2,533,821 (pre-rebind) -> 2,760,481 (#577, +8.9%) -> 2,334,205 (#584): 7.9% below the pre-rebind figure and 15.4% below the number #584 was opened to beat. The forced-order row `accepts_late_forced_order_as_out_of_window_source_event` went 3,194,009 -> 3,034,025 (#577, -5.0%) -> 2,538,180 (#584).

Two changes account for the fall, and they are separable. (1) The **single-anchor multi-field opening**: `field_opening_v1` now exposes `anchored_native_tx`, which verifies the thread's anchor once and hands back an opaque `AnchoredNativeTxV1` that `anchored_field_view`/`anchored_field_walk` open any number of fields against. Q21 is the wave's first script to read three things off one transaction — the scalar `validity_code`, field 0 and field 2 — and it was re-deriving the transaction id from the compact bytes for each, at roughly 211k mem apiece. It now derives it once. The guards #577 refused to give up for this saving are still in force and are still re-run **per field opened**: `carriage_reaches_the_anchor` and the §2.5 body/witness pairing both live in `field_pairs_with`, which every opening goes through. That is asserted rather than asserted-by-comment — the four `one_anchor_*` rows in `lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/field-opening-v1.test.ak` cover the positive two-field open, a field carried with another field's preimage, and the §2.5 refusal on both the view and the walk entry points. (2) The **retirement of `transaction_commitment`** from `L2TransactionSourceV1` and `ForcedInclusionTxV1`: the committed source value is 34 CBOR bytes shorter, so every vector in this module serialises, hashes and MPF-inserts less. That is the whole of the forced-order row's movement, which opens no field at all. Review cost, stated rather than absorbed: splitting `field_pairs_with` from one `and {}` into two separate asserts, so a refusal names the guard that fired, costs a measured +701 mem per opening — +1,402 on the two-field L2 row, 0 on the forced-order row, and the same +701 inside every per-opening figure `native-tx-q1x-exec-ledger-v1.json` and `native-tx-q31-exec-ledger-v1.json` publish. Both rows here include it.

NO new unbounded walk is introduced: the door's O(N) walk is over the same preimage the retired decode already walked, and the retired path additionally re-encoded every item, so there is no `basisFit:"exceeds"` row and no infeasibility string. What these rows do NOT claim is a cardinality envelope: each is one vector at one spend input and one output, and the family's cost at high cardinality is dominated by the per-item MPF delete/insert in `apply_l2_spends`/`apply_l2_outputs`, which this lane does not touch and does not measure. Rows are whole-test readings taken through `run-focused-check.mjs`, so they include fixture construction as well as validator execution — the same convention `native-tx-q31-exec-ledger-v1.json` uses, and the reason a row moves when a fixture is simplified. Regenerate with `MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN=<fork> node scripts/verify-q21-exec-ledger-v1.mjs --update`, and move any reported number in the same commit. Provisional: formal closure is Phase 7's, against the Phase-6 blueprint. `--update` rewrites the raw mem/cpu rows; it does NOT rewrite `basisFit`, and it is not a bypass — structural failures (a row or selector that did not run, or a fresh reading that contradicts a `within` judgement by exceeding the basis) fail in update mode too and the ledger is not rewritten.

**#586 re-take.** The L2 row moved once more, by **+1,312 mem / +358,482 cpu**, and the forced-order row did not move at all. The cause is #586's §5.3 ledger-key work: `decode_midgard_tx_input_cbor` in `lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/native-tx/components.ak` now asserts an input item is **exactly** 38 bytes (`midgard_tx_input_item_bytes`) before reading anything, which is what makes the non-minimal 39-byte spelling `82 ‖ 59 0020 ‖ tx_id(32) ‖ 19 index_be16` fail rather than decode to the same `(tx_id, output_index)` as the canonical item and give one out-ref two ledger-trie keys. The whole of the increase is that one length equality, so it is charged **per execution that decodes an out-ref, not per item**: the L2 row performs exactly one such decode (its field-0 positional read — field 2 is outputs and decodes no input), and the forced-order row performs none, which is why one row moved and the other is unchanged to the unit. The same +1,312 / +358,482 appears in `native-tx-q31-exec-ledger-v1.json`'s step-02 row and in all four door rows of `native-tx-q1x-exec-ledger-v1.json`, at 1 and at 296 spend inputs alike — identical at both cardinalities, which is what carries the per-execution claim. Against the pre-rebind 2,533,821 the L2 row now stands 7.8% below rather than the 7.9% of #584's reading; it moves no `basisFit`, and +1,312 is under 0.01% of the §3.3 memory basis.

**Re-taken under #587, one row, and for a serialization reason rather than a logic one.** #587 retired the counted publication receipt chain, which took `terminal_receipt_reference` out of `ledger_state.TxOrderPayloadV1`. Only the forced-order row reads that datum, and only `accepts_late_forced_order_as_out_of_window_source_event` builds one: it moved 2,538,180 -> 2,530,856 mem (-7,324) and 1,117,434,782 -> 1,115,127,417 cpu (-2,307,365) — the cost of one fewer `Option<OutputReference>` field to construct and destructure on the way to `tx_order_compact_body`. No other row in this ledger reads `TxOrderPayloadV1`, and none of them moved. The `basisFit` judgement is unchanged: the row was and remains far inside the 13.2M basis, and the movement is a small improvement, so nothing this ledger concludes turns on it.

**#592 round-4 re-take, §8.3 erratum E1's repair of `K` (15,900 → 15,148).** The L2 row moved by **+4,248 mem / +1,333,602 cpu** — 2,335,517 → 2,339,765 mem and 997,073,446 → 998,407,048 cpu, 0.18 % of the row — and the forced-order row, which opens no field, did not move. The cause is the door's own `expected_chunk_count` / chunk-offset arithmetic running against the repaired divisor rather than any change in what this lane measures. The per-opening decomposition of that total is NOT settled by these readings and is published as measured rather than derived. The L2 row opens the door twice and both fields are **body** fields (field 0 spend inputs, field 2 outputs), and a single body opening measures +2,224 mem / +682,801 cpu — in both rows of `native-tx-q31-exec-ledger-v1.json` and on the Q10/Q11 rows of `native-tx-q1x-exec-ledger-v1.json` — which would predict +4,448 / +1,365,602 here. What is measured instead is exactly twice the +2,124 / +666,801 that the same re-take puts on the *witness*-field rows of the Q1x ledger. Both of those are readings, not derivations, and nothing established here explains why two openings on this row come out 100 mem and 16,000 cpu apiece below the single-opening body figure; so the row value is the record and no per-opening rate is claimed for it. It moves no `basisFit` — the row was and remains far inside the 13.2M basis — and every conclusion this note draws about the rebind holds at the new figure: 2,339,765 against the pre-rebind 2,533,821, 7.7 % below it rather than the 7.8 % of #586's reading.

basis.source: GOAL_SPEC §3.3 — 20% margin off the supported L1 floor MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.minSupportedL1MaxTxMemoryUnits of 16,500,000 mem. Provenance, exactly as §3.3 states it: the captured in-repo artifact is the mainnet parameter snapshot in docs/midgard/decisions/0001-cardano-l1-transaction-capability-floor.md, Conway epoch 645, observed 2026-07-24. The report that the cap is unchanged at epoch 648 is corroboration only — no protocol-params artifact in this repository pins epoch 648.

modules.neutralisationNote: Every selector is mutation-verified rather than assumed, and each is listed against the mutation that turns it red. The two rebound call sites need different vectors, so both sets are here. #584 moved the L2 row's anchor check behind `anchored_native_tx` and its per-field guards behind `field_pairs_with`, and left every mutation below pointing at the same source lines it always did — the door's hash check and the anchor's id check are unmoved, and `field_pairs_with` is a guard no vector in THIS module can trip (both fields it opens are body fields under tier-1 carriage), which is why its selectors live in `field_opening_v1.test` instead. (1) and (2), `rejects_l2_transaction_with_a_substituted_spend_inputs_preimage` and `rejects_l2_transaction_with_a_substituted_outputs_preimage`: neutralising `whole_view`'s `expect field_commitment(preimage) == expected_hash` in `lib/midgard/native-tx-field-access-v1.ak` turns exactly these two red and nothing else in the module — they hold the §7.1 authenticate-once check for the L2 row's two door openings. (3) `rejects_l2_transaction_with_wrong_authenticated_transaction_id`: neutralising the anchor check `expect native_tx_id_for_version(version, body_cbor) == native_tx_id` in `lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/native-tx/compact.ak` turns exactly this one red. That check is what BOTH rebound call sites rest on — the L2 row's `verify_native_tx_compact_cbor_v1` and the forced-order row's `tx_order_compact_body` — and no door selector sees it, because the door is reached only once the anchor has been accepted. (4) `accepts_omitted_forced_order_at_authenticated_end_time_boundary`: the forced-order row asserts `!forced_event_is_due(...)`, so a due-check degenerating to always-False would satisfy that row for free; forcing `forced_event_is_due` to False turns exactly this selector red and leaves every other test in the module green, selector (5) included. It is a positive test used as a neutralisation selector for precisely that reason — the vacuity direction of a negated guard is only provable by a test that needs the guard to say yes. (5) `rejects_omitted_forced_order_published_after_challenged_block`: forcing `forced_event_is_due` to True turns this, `rejects_omitted_forced_order_at_excluded_start_time_boundary` and the forced-order row itself red. It brackets the authenticated window from the other side, at the same `end_time + 1` inclusion time the row is measured at. Two vectors are deliberately NOT listed, both because they survive the door mutation: `rejects_l2_transaction_with_uncommitted_spend_preimage`, because `apply_l2_spends` rejects its mismatched delete witness before the door is ever the reason, and `rejects_l2_transaction_with_a_miscounted_committed_spend_inputs_preimage`, which two independent door guards refuse, so it isolates neither.
